knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Compiled execution semantics diverge from eager API validation for invalid index inputs
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Compiler transformations may replace strict API-level input validation with lower-level primitives that accept broader input semantics, causing eager and compiled modes to disagree.

risk_dimensions.shape: Target dimension sizes where out-of-range or negative indices could alias valid positions under lower-level wrapping semantics
risk_dimensions.dtype: Integer index tensors, especially int64, may expose code paths with different validation behavior
risk_dimensions.device: CPU, CUDA, and MPS backends may follow different decomposition or validation paths
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Eager execution versus compiled/optimized execution modes

failure_mechanism.description: A compiled backend can lower the API operation into a more permissive indexing primitive that accepts negative index values, bypassing the API-level validation that rejects them in eager mode.

input_exploration: Vary index values from valid non-negative values to negative boundary values near the negative dimension size
Mix positive and negative indices within the same index tensor
Vary input tensor shapes and the target dimension being indexed
Test dense and non-contiguous input tensors where applicable
constraint_awareness: Eager API validation may reject negative indices while compiled backends accept them
Index tensors usually require integer dtypes such as int64
Compiled-mode decompositions can differ across backends and devices
Identical inputs must be executed in both eager and compiled modes before comparing outcomes
oracle_strategy: Flag execution mismatches where eager mode raises an exception but compiled mode succeeds
Compare outputs between eager and compiled executions for identical inputs
Treat exception presence or absence and output inconsistency as contract violation signals

transferability.reason: The principle that compile-time decompositions can weaken or alter eager API input validation applies broadly to indexing, slicing, selection, and shape manipulation operations. Comparing eager and compiled behavior for boundary inputs is a general testing strategy across many tensor APIs.

important_considerations: Prioritize boundary index values that expose validation mismatches between eager and compiled execution
Cover multiple backends and devices when feasible because decomposition behavior may differ
Do not assume eager and compiled modes share identical input validation contracts
Target APIs whose decompositions may lower to more permissive indexing or data movement primitives
generation_strategy: Generate harnesses that execute the same API call with boundary-condition inputs in both eager and compiled modes, then compare exceptions and outputs. Vary indices across valid and invalid ranges to reveal contract divergence without copying historical bug values.
